answer:
Based on the analysis performed on your uploaded `dem.tif` file:

## Mean Slope

The mean slope of the 30 m DEM is **5.75°** (5.7534°), computed using the standard Horn's method slope algorithm (the same used by ArcGIS/QGIS). 

- Median slope: 5.82°
- Slope range: 0.57° to 5.82°
- Mean slope in percent: ~10.1%

The DEM is in UTM 16N (EPSG:32616), with 30 m resolution, 200×150 cells, and elevations ranging from 200.3 m to 496.7 m.

## Watershed Area

The watershed draining to the outlet at 40.04950° N, 88.26302° W (UTM 16N x=392265, y=4434015) has an area of **15.85 km²** (15.8517 km²).

This was delineated using the standard D8 flow-direction method (pysheds, with depression filling and flat resolution):
- 17,613 of the 18,000 DEM cells drain to this outlet
- The outlet cell was snapped to the highest flow-accumulation cell at the southern boundary
- The watershed spans roughly 40.049°N to 40.082°N, 88.29°W to 88.24°W

**Important caveat:** Because the outlet sits exactly on the DEM's southern boundary, the delineated watershed is truncated by the DEM extent — the true watershed draining to that point likely extends beyond the DEM to the south. The 15.85 km² is the area *within this DEM* that drains to the outlet.

## Deliverables

- **Interactive map layer**: "Watershed draining to outlet (40.0495N, 88.263W)" — the watershed polygon is plotted and clickable on your live map.
- **Downloadable GeoJSON**: [watershed.geojson](https://agent/files/file_cb029103ad0c/download) (15.85 km², 17,613 cells)
- **Static map image**: [watershed_map.png](https://agent/files/file_87e934071e5f/download)

Note: the `terrain_derivative` tool initially misread this DEM's resolution (treated it as a single ~3,340 km pixel and returned slope 0), so the slope was computed directly with the standard algorithm instead.
